title: Turkey, light meat, roasted, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey is a large bird native to North America. Light turkey meat, roasted without skin, has a mild flavor, low fat content, and a high amount of protein. It is commonly used in dietetic meals and dishes where a light texture and neutral taste are desired.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkeys were domesticated by Native Americans more than 2,000 years ago.
Light turkey meat contains less fat than dark meat and is often chosen for low‑calorie diets.
Roasting without skin retains most nutrients while reducing saturated fat.
Turkey is a traditional Thanksgiving dish in the USA, but its popularity is growing in Russia as a healthy protein source.
Turkey meat is rich in tryptophan, an amino acid that supports serotonin production.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Light turkey meat provides about 30 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Roasted skin‑less turkey contains less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey supplies vitamin B6, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The meat provides selenium, zinc, and phosphorus, essential for immune function and bone health.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of high protein and moderate calories helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bird meat.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked turkey can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C.

items.title: High sodium in processed preparations
items.content: When using pre‑made marinades or sauces, watch the salt content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted light turkey can be sliced for sandwiches, added to salads, tossed with pasta, or used as a protein base in various dishes. It stores well in the fridge and can be reheated quickly in a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked turkey in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it retains quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
